clue.text: Steal in the ears as Dalek's voice?

parts.note: to rob is to steal
otic is the anatomical adjective for things relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A puzzling image of theft taking place inside the ears, set beside the grating voice of a Doctor Who villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Daleks are the metal-cased aliens of the British TV series Doctor Who, famous for their harsh, mechanical voices.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalek speaks in a flat, machine-like tone, the kind of delivery described as mechanical.

clue.text: Check votes again in detail

definitions.meaning: after a close election the ballots are counted a second time
to ... a story is to tell it in full, narrate it

explanation.surface: An election official asks for the ballots to be gone through again, item by item.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a second tally of ballots; the other is a verb meaning to narrate in full.

clue.text: Supporters start to save money

parts.note: bras are undergarments that support

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of save

explanation.surface: Backers are urged to begin putting cash aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans or backers, but here it means underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for cash, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Article cheers European character

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A newspaper article salutes some colourful person from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and Greece is in Europe, so a European written symbol.

clue.text: Wild idea to correspond with artist

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree or correspond with it
RA stands for Royal Academician, a British artist

explanation.surface: A fanciful notion happens to tally with what a painter has in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera, from the mythical composite monster, is a fanciful or impossible notion.

clue.text: City needs a good hospital — 500 coming in sick

indicators.note: the group of letters enters the word for sick, sitting inside it

parts.note: bad means ill, as in feeling bad
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A city's health service needs a decent hospital to cope with five hundred patients arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts AGHD inside BAD, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: Actor Brian shed blood around ship

indicators.note: the bleeding word is wrapped around the ship abbreviation

parts.note: to bleed is to shed blood
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A well-known actor is wounded aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Blessed is a booming-voiced English actor, known for Flash Gordon and Blackadder.

clue.text: Development in East got rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together anew, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A property project in the east of a city was reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the period of growth of an embryo, hence any slow coming-into-being of a plan.

clue.text: Port only provides fish

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel ferry port in Kent
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A single harbour town is the only supplier of seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatfish, named after the Kent port, is a prized European species.

clue.text: Extremely dirty and repulsive house

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant, repulsive

explanation.surface: A filthy, disgusting home.
explanation.definitionFit: A house can mean a ruling family line, like the House of Windsor; a succession of rulers from one family.

clue.text: Eire faces uneasy truce

indicators.note: uneasy suggests unsettled, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Ireland confronts an anxious pause in hostilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is an agreed halt to fighting, the same as a truce.

clue.text: Cardinal in south quits

parts.note: to be quits is to be even, owing nothing

explanation.surface: A senior churchman in the south resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but a cardinal number is a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, of which this is one.

clue.text: Divert attention from London-bound coach?

definitions.meaning: to steal the limelight from another performer
up is the direction of travel towards London, and a stagecoach is a coach

explanation.surface: A passenger on a bus to the capital steals the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw notice away from someone, originally by moving upstage so they must face away; and a stagecoach heading to the capital.

clue.text: Greek victor going inside roasts nuts

indicators.note: the victor letter enters the rearranged word
nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek winner heads into the kitchen to roast some nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns ROASTS into STAROS, and 'going inside' puts V into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavros is a common Greek man's name.

clue.text: Writing after interval, news can be so old

indicators.note: the writing word is placed after the interval word

parts.note: a third is a musical interval
hand means handwriting, as in a neat hand

explanation.surface: A pause before writing, with a remark that news grows stale.
explanation.definitionFit: News passed on through several people before reaching you is stale and secondhand or worse.

clue.text: One sten gun shot bags resistance rebel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or hold, so the rearranged letters hold the resistance symbol
shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A single Sten gun fired captures the resistance fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges STENGUN to NSUGENT and 'bags' puts R inside it. A Sten gun was a British wartime submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent rises in revolt against authority.

clue.text: Velocity rising with single step in void

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: speed is velocity
a pace is one stride

explanation.surface: Speed builds with each footstep into nothingness.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast emptiness between stars and galaxies is the void of outer space.

clue.text: Dramatic device from smooth Yankee

parts.note: to iron is to smooth out creases
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A theatrical trick borrowed from a suave American.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic irony, where the audience knows more than the characters, is a stage technique.

clue.text: Former potentate at last getting stick

parts.note: past means former, as in past presidents

indicators.note: at the end, so take the closing letter of potentate

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler finally gets a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is glue, and to stick is to glue.

clue.text: Aesop mixed up thick broth

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so these letters are stirred together

explanation.surface: The fable writer stirs together a hearty stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed up' reads as one anagram signal, but only 'mixed' works on the fabulist's name; the final word stays put at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick soup of dried split peas, also slang for dense London fog.

clue.text: Martial arts student, inexperienced, given punch

parts.note: green means naive or untried
to belt someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A raw karate pupil gets thumped.
explanation.definitionFit: In some martial arts a green sash marks a low-ranked learner; by extension, the learner wearing it.

clue.text: Brave man to vex six-footer?

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or vex
an ant is an insect, and insects have six feet

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow annoys a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a dashing, chivalrous man, and as an adjective the word means brave.

clue.text: Soubriquet's essence in letter written up

indicators.note: the essence word is placed within the reversed letter name
in a down entry, written up means set down from bottom to top

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
pith is the core or essence of something

explanation.surface: The heart of a nickname is recorded in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses the spelt-out name of the letter T, and 'in' places the essence within it. The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubriquet is a nickname or descriptive tag, as is an epithet.

clue.text: Greek hero recognised in Florida and Georgia?

definitions.meaning: the Athenian who slew the Minotaur
both states lie in the south-east of America, read as three words

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek hero is spotted in two southern American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE SE US: Florida and Georgia are in the south-east United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the mythical Athenian king who killed the Minotaur in the labyrinth.

clue.text: Mister Solo animated after a little hesitation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the opening pieces

parts.note: er is the sound of a slight pause in speech

indicators.note: animated means set in lively motion, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mr Solo springs into action after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title, as in Han Solo; it is something that produces mist. 'animated' rearranges SOLO to OSOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a spray can, a device that releases a fine mist.

clue.text: Think pigmies occasionally must conceal a trap

indicators.note: the alternate letters must hide the other pieces within them
occasionally means every so often, so take alternate letters

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Consider that small people sometimes have to hide a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes IME from pigmies, and 'must conceal' puts AGIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to suppose or think, as in 'I imagine so'.

clue.text: Subtle charm of an Italian city

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, like an
Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: The understated allure of a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma can mean a faint pervasive quality or air, a subtle attraction.

clue.text: Freezing in panic in Gdansk

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Cold weather causes alarm in a Polish port.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the formation of ice, as on an aircraft wing in freezing conditions.

clue.text: Work period for Peter Grimes?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A spell of labour for a man called Peter Grimes.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Grimes looks like a person, but it is Benjamin Britten's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Grimes is an example: an opera by Benjamin Britten about a Suffolk fisherman.

clue.text: Olympian collapsed in pit — oh dear!

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete falls down into a hole, prompting a cry of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges PITOHDEAR. 'Olympian' suggests an athlete; it is a god of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite, goddess of love, is one of the gods who dwelt on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Job description from one in surgery?

definitions.meaning: the biblical Job was proverbial for his long-suffering endurance
a person under a doctor's care; surgery is the British word for a doctor's office

explanation.surface: An employer's role specification provided by someone in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like employment, but it is the biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Job is the byword for endurance, which describes him; and a person receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: Something very irritating in opening chatter

parts.note: a tear is a rip or opening
gas is idle talk, chatter

explanation.surface: An annoying thing turns up in someone's introductory small talk.
explanation.definitionFit: This riot-control chemical stings the eyes and throat, an irritant in the literal sense.
